title: Charles Elcock to D'Arcy Thompson, 6–8 March 1884: exact archive locator and Challenger extraction target

repository.institution: University of St Andrews Libraries and Museums
repository.extent: 2 autograph letters signed, 3pp to 4pp, plus 1 rubbing image, 1p

catalogue_supported_content.main_theme: Archaeology/antiquarian study, especially authenticity of a medal allegedly found in a peat bog at Oughterard, County Kildare.
catalogue_supported_content.natural_history_component: General discussion of Irish specimens, studies and developments.
catalogue_supported_content.document_note: The St Andrews catalogue identifies ms21974 as a rubbing image of the medal, 1p. The catalogue groups the two letters and rubbing under ms21974-ms21975; it does not expose a transcript of the Challenger passage in the indexed public description.

what_is_now_secure: Elcock personally corresponded with D'Arcy Thompson in March 1884.
The archive catalogue explicitly states that these letters refer to Challenger expedition samples.
The correspondence is contemporaneous with Elcock's active foraminiferal preparation work and predates the 1885 Type Slide advertising evidence already in the corpus.
This is a direct archival route into Elcock's Challenger relation rather than a later auction-family attribution.
what_is_not_yet_secure: Who supplied the Challenger samples to Elcock.
Which Challenger stations, localities, depths or sample numbers were involved.
What type of material was sent.
Whether the samples were supplied for identification, mounting, comparison, sale, exchange or another purpose.
Whether any Challenger-derived material entered the commercial Type Slides.
Whether the material described in these letters can be identified with any Whipple, Flints or other surviving Elcock object.

image_transcription_request.request: Page images or a transcription of ms21974-ms21975, preserving page order, versos, enclosures and any marginal annotations.
extract_verbatim_fields: named intermediaries such as Murray or museum staff
references to labels, lists, parcels or prior correspondence
image_transcription_request.guard: Keep medal/rubbing discussion analytically separate from the natural-history passage unless the letters themselves connect them.

related_independent_evidence.relation: Whipple states that Elcock's retained working/reference archive contains material from Challenger, Porcupine and Knight Errant surveys.

related_independent_evidence.source: Belfast Municipal Art Gallery and Museum, Quarterly Notes, no. XVI, June 1910, obituary
related_independent_evidence.relation: Later institutional obituary states that Challenger Deep-Sea Dredging Expedition samples were forwarded to Elcock for examination; original text remains a separate verification target.

research_payoff: The question has narrowed from whether Elcock handled Challenger material to what exactly the March 1884 letters say about that handling. If the letters name source, station/sample or scientific purpose, the expedition-material bridge can move from catalogue-level relation to a first-order transaction/workflow chain.
